reasons.reproducibility: Whole-lake H2O2 dosing (after lab and enclosure tests) needs permits and field equipment.
reasons.effectiveness: Cyanobacteria and microcystin fell 99% within days and stayed low for 7 weeks.
reasons.environment: H2O2 was gone within days and most non-target groups were largely unaffected.

reasons.reproducibility: Flasks are simple, but it uses PSP-toxic Alexandrium catenella, 300 L mesocosms and mussel saxitoxin assays.
reasons.effectiveness: -17-74% at 2-3 d and -42-96% at ~1 wk; kelp gave -73% in 48 h in mesocosms, though total chlorophyll did not fall.
reasons.cost: Mesocosms and saxitoxin analysis put it at $500-5,000.
reasons.environment: Seaweed is retrievable, but Ulva pushed pH to 9.0-9.5 (sometimes >10) and other algae replaced the target.

reasons.reproducibility: Stocking 3.2 million clams across 64 plots in Shinnecock Bay is field-scale and needs permits.
reasons.effectiveness: Brown tide fell from 0.3-1.9x10^6 to <10^4 cells/mL, but the link is correlational with no control bay.
reasons.cost: Millions of clams and years of surveys exceed $5,000.
reasons.environment: Native clams added; clam densities rose 18x and harvests 16x with no harm reported.

reasons.reproducibility: Typical reviewed lab work needs surface-modified clays that must be prepared or sourced with a sponsor.
reasons.effectiveness: Modified clays remove HAB cells far better than natural clay and are widely used in China, but no percent is given.
reasons.cost: Lab-scale modified clay trials are roughly $150-500.
reasons.environment: Clay is applied at 4-10 t/km^2, settles to the seabed and is never retrieved, despite the authors' no-harm claim.

reasons.reproducibility: A field trial in a disused UK canal, so field-scale.
reasons.effectiveness: Reported only that straw reduced filamentous algae; no numbers or controls seen in the secondary summary.
reasons.cost: Dose not seen; straw is cheap but canal-scale use scored conservatively at $150-500.
reasons.time: Duration not seen; the summary calls it a long-term method, so seasons.
reasons.environment: Not reported; rotting straw is removable but its decomposition may lower oxygen.

reasons.reproducibility: Bench cultures of Microcystis with common oxidants, but ozone generation and cell-integrity (flow cytometry) need a sponsor.
reasons.effectiveness: Chlorine compromised >=88% of cells within 1 minute and 6 mg/L ozone lysed 90% in 5 minutes.
reasons.cost: Culture, oxidants and cell-integrity assays are roughly $150-500.
reasons.environment: All oxidants burst cells and released intracellular toxins, and copper sulphate adds a persistent metal.
